metadata.title: 1969 Case 07
metadata.original_presentation: A fifty-six-year-old woman was admitted to the hospital because of a cough, fever and pain in the chest.

required.content: What is the patient's history of alcohol use?
required.response: She had begun to imbibe alcohol heavily at the time of her husband's death five years previously and increased her intake during the year before entry.

teaching_points.content: Chronic alcohol use can lead to immunosuppression and increase the risk of infections such as pneumonia.

required.content: What were the patient's symptoms prior to admission?
required.response: Nine months before admission there was the onset of agitation and a progressively severe cough with hemoptysis. She was anorectic, with a loss of 40 pounds in weight. Persistent pleuritic pain in the right anterior portion of the chest developed, accompanied by a cough productive of rusty, mucoid sputum. She had intermittent episodes of fever, chills and sweats.

teaching_points.content: Weight loss and hemoptysis in a patient with chronic cough and fever may suggest a serious underlying condition such as tuberculosis or malignancy.

required.content: Does the patient have any known allergies?

teaching_points.content: Knowledge of drug allergies is crucial in selecting appropriate antibiotic therapy.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Lung cancer
refuting_evidence: intermittent fever, chills, and sweats are less typical

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Pneumonia
supporting_evidence: cough productive of rusty, mucoid sputum

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Alcoholic lung disease
refuting_evidence: fever, chills, and sweats are less typical

required.content: What were the findings on physical examination upon admission?
required.response: The patient was cachectic and dehydrated. The mouth was dry, and the teeth were carious. A small, firm lymph node was palpable in the right posterior cervical region. Coarse rhonchi were audible over the anterior and posterior portions of the right lung field; there was no friction rub. The heart was normal; no murmur or friction rub was heard. The liver and spleen were not enlarged, no tenderness was elicited in the abdomen, and the bowel sounds were present. There was no clubbing or edema of the extremities, and no petechiae were seen. Neurologic examination was negative.

teaching_points.content: Cachexia and dehydration can indicate chronic illness and poor nutritional status, which may complicate recovery.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Tuberculosis
supporting_evidence: persistent pleuritic pain in the right anterior portion of the chest
intermittent episodes of fever, chills, and sweats
coarse rhonchi over the right lung field

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Lung cancer
supporting_evidence: persistent pleuritic pain in the right anterior portion of the chest
small, firm lymph node in the right posterior cervical region

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Pneumonia
supporting_evidence: cough productive of rusty, mucoid sputum
coarse rhonchi over the right lung field

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Alcoholic lung disease
refuting_evidence: no specific lung findings typical of alcoholic lung disease

required.content: What were the initial laboratory test results?
required.response: The urine had a specific gravity of 1.033 and gave a + test for protein; the sediment contained 5 to 8 white cells per high-power field. The hematocrit was 42 per cent, and the white-cell count 23,500, with 82 per cent neutrophils and 5 per cent band forms. The urea nitrogen was 16 mg, the glucose 180 mg, the calcium 8.8 mg, the phosphorus 2.9 mg, and the protein 5.5 gm (the albumin 3.2 gm, and the globulin 2.3 gm) per 100 ml. The sodium was 137 mEq, and the potassium 3.1 mEq per liter.

teaching_points.content: Leukocytosis with a left shift is indicative of an acute bacterial infection.

required.content: What were the findings from the chest x-ray?
required.response: An x-ray film of the chest revealed almost complete collapse of the left lower lobe and an amorphous infiltrate in the right lower lobe; the lungs were otherwise clear, and the heart and aorta were normal; there was a small right pleural effusion.

teaching_points.content: Lobar collapse and infiltrates on chest x-ray can indicate pneumonia or other pulmonary pathology.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Pneumonia
supporting_evidence: infiltrate in right lower lobe on chest x-ray
additional_information_needed: consideration of atypical pathogens given chronicity

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Tuberculosis
refuting_evidence: no cavitary lesions noted on chest x-ray
additional_information_needed: sputum acid-fast bacilli (AFB) smear and culture

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Lung Cancer
supporting_evidence: small, firm lymph node in cervical region
refuting_evidence: no mass noted on chest x-ray

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Alcoholic Lung Disease
refuting_evidence: no specific radiological findings typical of alcoholic lung disease
additional_information_needed: evaluation for other alcohol-related organ damage

required.content: What treatments were administered during the hospital stay?
required.response: Erythromycin was administered intravenously. Diazepam (Valium) was administered intravenously, and the trachea was intubated. Intermittent positive-pressure respiration was instituted, and digoxin and aminophylline were given. Diazepam was continued, and diphenylhydantoin was added to the regimen. Plasma was administered.

teaching_points.content: Management of respiratory distress and seizures involves airway protection, seizure control, and addressing the underlying cause.
